identity.name: East Hebei Autonomous Council
native_names: 冀東防共自治政府 (Jìdōng Fánggòng Zìzhì Zhèngfǔ)

land.text: the Tanggu Truce demilitarised zone, 'the 22 counties in Hebei province' between the Great Wall and Beijing-Tianjin
'absorbed ... into the collaborationist Provisional Government of China in February 1938'

capitals.name: Tongzhou (now in Beijing)
capitals.note: The page: Yin Ju-keng proclaimed 'to have their capital at Tongzhou' on 25 November 1935. Coordinates are the modern Tongzhou district.

correction.text: the demilitarised zone south of the Great Wall: 22 counties of east Hebei with the capital Tongzhou

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for this council (the Republic of China and Empire of Japan dossiers draw it from Cliopatria's Japan growth). 'The 22 counties in Hebei province' of the demilitarised zone, which 'extends 100 km south of the Great Wall from Beijing to Tianjin' (Tanggu Truce page); the pages list no counties, so a six-point ring from Tongzhou to Shanhaiguan stands for it. No infobox area. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, at the reviewer's request: the ring's southern edge was pulled north: its south-west corner from 39.0 N to 39.55 N and its southern vertex from 38.9 N to 39.3 N, so that Tianjin city (117.2 E, 39.13 N) now lies outside it. Both pages re-read: the Tanggu Truce page defines the zone as 'extending 100 km south of the Great Wall from Beijing to Tianjin' and says nothing on whether either city is inside; the East Hebei page says the 22 counties were 'extending from Tianjin to Beiping' and does not mention Tangshan. The reviewer's statement that Tianjin stayed under the Chinese Hebei-Chahar authorities is not on either page (I disagree that it is page-supported); the move follows from the 100 km rule (the Great Wall runs at 40.4-40.8 N between Beijing and Shanhaiguan, so a line 100 km south of it is near 39.5 N at Beijing and 39.1 N at the coast) and from Tianjin being named as the zone's end, not part of it. The ring is still a reading.]

region.text: 22 counties of east Hebei, capital Tongzhou

ledger.note: 1935: Yin Ju-keng proclaims the East Hebei council. The page dates the proclamation of autonomy to 15 November 1935 and independence 'from' the Nanjing government to 25 November 1935; the zone had been 'purged' of Kuomintang influence by the Tanggu Truce and the 1935 He-Umezu Agreement. The page is silent on the counties.

region.text: 22 counties of east Hebei, capital Tongzhou

ledger.note: 25 November 1935: the council is Japan's client from its declaration of independence. 'It has been described by historians as either a Japanese puppet state or a buffer state'; 'The new government immediately signed economic and military treaties with Japan'; the page also calls it 'the pro-Japanese collaborationist regime'. The page hedges between puppet and buffer, so confidence 2. Recorded from the vassal's side (east-hebei-autonomous-council is the vassal, empire-of-japan the suzerain); the Japan dossier carries the mirror event with counterpart east-hebei-autonomous-council (empire-of-japan /ledger/44). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added at the reviewer's request (check 3, vassal mirror); page re-read the same day.]

region.text: 22 counties of east Hebei, capital Tongzhou

ledger.note: February 1938: the relation ends when the council is 'absorbed into the collaborationist Provisional Government of China in February 1938' (infobox 1935-1938). The land stays under a Japanese client in Beijing (the Provisional Government), which the Japan dossier records as its own relation. Mirror of empire-of-japan /ledger/48. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added.]

February 1938: East Hebei is absorbed. 'absorbed into the collaborationist Provisional Government of China in February 1938' (the page gives no day); the Provisional Government itself was established on 14 December 1937 (Provisional Government page, which does not itself mention the absorption).

wars.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
wars.outcome: The Tanggu Truce proved 'only a temporary respite until hostilities erupted again in 1937'; East Hebei was absorbed into the Provisional Government in February 1938, after the war began.
wars.note: Only the opening of the war touches this council's life; the Second Sino-Japanese War article itself was not opened for this dossier.

certainty.note: A buffer zone with no surveyed line on any page opened; the 100 km depth is the Tanggu Truce's own figure.

sources.title: East Hebei Autonomous Council
sources.note: Dates 15 and 25 November 1935, February 1938; capital Tongzhou; '22 counties'; buffer between Manchukuo and China. Re-read 2026-10-25: 'Japanese puppet state or a buffer state'; economic and military treaties with Japan; '22 counties in Hebei province ... extending from Tianjin to Beiping'; survived the Tongzhou mutiny of late July 1937.

sources.title: Provisional Government of the Republic of China (1937-1940)
sources.note: Established 14 December 1937 at Beijing; merged into the Reorganized National Government on 30 March 1940; the page does not mention East Hebei's absorption.

sources.title: Tanggu Truce
sources.note: 31 May 1933: the demilitarised zone 100 km south of the Great Wall from Beijing to Tianjin; de facto recognition of Manchukuo. Re-read 2026-10-25: the page does not say whether Beijing or Tianjin lies inside the zone; public order by a lightly armed Demilitarized Zone Peace Preservation Corps.

notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from three pages (a 3-year state, below the ten-year bar, written because the Republic of China (ea-08-c) and Empire of Japan (jk-01-d) dossiers name it by slug). Not settled: the 22 counties are not listed on any page (a ring stands in); the page gives no founding tenure for Yin Ju-keng; the Tongzhou mutiny of July 1937 is named on the page without detail, and who held the land between that and February 1938 is not on the page. The Tanggu Truce date (31 May 1933) and the 100 km zone are on the Tanggu Truce page, which does not mention an East Hebei government. Gazetteer: Tongzhou is missing as a place name (it is inside Beijing). The slug of the absorbing government is provisional-government-of-the-republic-of-china.

[ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, after the adversarial review (verdict fail)] (1) Added vassal_start empire-of-japan (1935-11) and vassal_end empire-of-japan (1938-2), from the vassal's side as in the kumul-khanate dossier; mirrors empire-of-japan /ledger/44 and /48. The East Hebei page hedges ('either a Japanese puppet state or a buffer state'), so the start is at confidence 2. (2) The ring (found region, dissolve region, successor land and the keyframe) was redrawn with its southern edge north of Tianjin: south-west corner (116.5 E, 39.55 N) and southern vertex (118.0 E, 39.3 N) instead of 39.0 and 38.9 N. I agree that the old ring put Tianjin inside the council, which no page says; I do not agree that the pages say Tianjin 'stayed under the Chinese Hebei-Chahar authorities' (the Tanggu Truce page is silent on whether either end city is inside the zone). The Fengtian, Zhili and Shanxi dossiers keep the old six-point corridor polygon for the Second Zhili-Fengtian War zone and the 1930 Northeast Army corridor (a different question: the Shanhaiguan to Beijing approaches), and I left those unchanged.
